meta.description: Eskom residential tariff components, used by the shadow dynamic retail price panel. Every figure is from Eskom's published Schedule of Standard Prices; nothing here is modelled.
meta.source: Eskom Schedule of Standard Prices for the 2026/27 financial year, effective 1 April 2026, published after NERSA's MYPD6 decision of 5 March 2026. Direct-customer rates, 8.76% average increase.
meta.vat: All figures INCLUDE VAT at 15% unless a field name says otherwise.
meta.phase_in: Eskom is moving residential cost recovery from energy charges to fixed charges over three years. Service and administration went from 33.33% fixed in FY2026 to 66.66% in FY2027. The Generation Capacity Charge went from 20% to 30%. The remainder of each sits inside the energy charge. The ERTSA application for 2027/28, gazetted 4 Sep 2026, continues this.
meta.why_this_file_exists: The shadow retail price needs the components a household actually pays, not a single average rate. It also lets the fixed/variable split be modelled as a scenario rather than asserted - see the frozen and completed cases in RESULTS.md.
meta.caveat_municipal: Homepower and Homelight are ESKOM DIRECT tariffs. Municipal customers buy from their distributor at a bulk rate and pay that distributor's own structure and markup, which varies by an order of magnitude between metros. Do not present an Eskom-direct figure as a national household price.

homepower4.description: Standard residential, 80 A single-phase, no grid-tied generation. The most common Eskom-direct residential tariff.
homepower4.energy_note: Flat rate. The same at 03:00 as at 18:00, and the same in July as in January. This is the quantity a dynamic tariff would replace.

phase_in_status.note: At 100% the service and administration charge is R9.90/day and the generation capacity charge R2.73/day. R5.21/day, about R159/month, has still to move from energy to fixed.

homepower4.fixed_r_per_month_note: R17.86/day x 30 = R535.8, quoted as R536. Eskom bills per day, so a 31-day month is R553.7 and a 28-day month R500.1. The monthly figure is a convenience for comparison, not a charge - use fixed_r_per_day for anything computed.

homeflex.description: Time-of-use residential. REQUIRED for any household with grid-tied generation, so every rooftop PV customer is on it.
homeflex.peak_definition: June to August, 06:00-09:00 and 17:00-20:00 on weekdays
homeflex.note: The existing evidence that South African households CAN be exposed to time-varying prices. The winter peak is 4.4x the off-peak rate, a wider spread than most dynamic tariffs abroad.

homelight60a.description: Prepaid, 60 A, no fixed charge at all.
homelight60a.note: Beats Homepower 4 at every realistic consumption level for eligible households, precisely because there is no fixed charge to absorb. A household on Homelight has nothing to gain from a dynamic tariff's fixed component and everything from its energy component.

reference_octopus_agile.description: Britain's most-cited dynamic tariff, included as a published comparator rather than a target. Its formula is public, which is the standard this model holds itself to.
reference_octopus_agile.structure: day-ahead wholesale, half-hourly, plus regional network costs, plus a peak uplift, plus margin, plus VAT, subject to a cap
reference_octopus_agile.note: The standing charge is NOT dynamic. That is the honest limit on what any dynamic tariff can shift, and it matters more in South Africa: a 200 kWh Homepower household is already at 43% fixed against Octopus's 24%.
